summary: Technology has become a mainstay of personal and public life and makes even monotonous tasks quicker and easier
Not everyone is comfortable with fast change; studies show that people who feel in control welcome it, while less confident people see it as a threat
Employees cannot avoid new technology at work, so workers must be trained effectively and practically so that they feel in control
The first step is to give employees the right mindset by assuring them they will gain from the change, which paves the way for greater developments
arguments: New technology makes even monotonous tasks quicker and easier
Studies show that how well people cope with new technology mirrors their character: confident people welcome change, less confident people feel threatened
Because employees cannot avoid new technology, effective and practical training is imperative so that they are in control
Giving workers the right mindset, by assuring them they will gain from the change, is a vital step for integrating humans and technology
arguments_main: Names effective, practical training of workers as the most important argument (the right mindset step is also acceptable)
Gives a reason from the text, e.g. it is the essay's answer to the workplace impasse, because less confident employees cannot avoid new technology
